rows.en:
The thing was already gone.
Was it because I'd let go of Shindo's hand{f:?|?}{p}

"I told you not to be startled.
Provoke it the wrong way and there's no telling what it'll do to you."
Saying that, Shindo pulled away.
"Wh-what was that..."
"The one I told you about earlier.
Looks like it's taken a liking to you."
"N... no way!"
As {f:I|I} panicked, Shindo gave me a cold look.
"That's what you get for setting up a project like this half for fun.
You're the one who called it here.
That thing's gonna follow you around from now on."
"No way!
Isn't there some way to get rid of it★"
"Sorry, I don't know any.
I've just got a bit more of a sixth sense than most people, that's all."
Shindo grinned.{p}

{f:I|I} was annoyed, but I kept quiet.
He was my senior, after all{f:.|.}
Shindo saw {f:me|me} like that and gave a wry smile.
"You're a good kid, but... I don't think you're cut out to be a reporter."
"...What do you mean by that?"
"Listen closely to what people say, and when something bugs you, dig in and ask.
That's the basics of being a reporter, right?
You can't do that."
That made {f:me|me} {f:genuinely angry|genuinely angry}.
"I don't think you have any right to say that to me."
My tone came out harsher than I meant.
"That's rude, isn't it?
Earlier, too, you tried to scare me, saying a ghost or something was watching {f:me|me}..."
Shindo chuckled.{p}

"So you thought I was just trying to scare you?
Guess your sixth sense isn't worth much either."{p}

"I thought you had a little more promise than that, but maybe I was wrong.
Kinda killed the mood for me.
So my story ends right here."
For an instant, something writhed beneath Shindo's face.
I couldn't make it out clearly, but it was definitely something evil.
Is this person really Makoto Shindo, a student at this school{f:?|?}{p}In the suffocating tension, {f:I|I} turned to face the last one.
I felt as if carrying on with this was the only way to keep my sanity...........{p}

Tch, what a wimp.
Well, I guess it might be a bit much for the kiddies.
Can't be helped, then.
Things didn't go as planned, but I'll tell you that story about playing cards I mentioned at the start.{p}
Still, you gotta admit they're really well made.{p}

For the record, I actually like 'em quite a bit.
I mean, they're really well made, right?{p}

That's a good thing.
If you're as sloppy as me, nothing good comes of it.
Then again, if I'd never met Okura, I'd never have ended up in that mess...
Whoops, I'm getting off track.{p}

{f:Don't lie to me|Hey}, {f:pal|you don't have to hide it}.
{f:A guy who hates gambling|Or maybe}{f: is no man at all| you've just never gambled}.
{f:Even I love it|I do it all the time, though}.
{f:Be honest|Tell me the truth}.{p}...{f:Or are you saying|So are you saying} you've never once made a bet in your life?
I've never gambled
Actually, I have

Huh!
{f:You're a rare one|So that's how it is}.
{f:Practically a protected species, aren't ya|I kinda figured, though}.
But {f:I wonder how long that'll last|you might get a chance to gamble one of these days}.{p}

...Well, whatever.
So anyway, Okura used to be an easy mark.
But at some point, that changed.
All of a sudden, he got really good at gambling.{p}

{f:See? Told ya|I see}.
{f:Act cool all you like|Put on airs all you like}, but that's how it goes{f:.|.}{p}

Ha ha, listen to you, admitting it yourself.
But gambling's all about the mind games, you know.
If you're that honest, it's probably not for you.
Or is that a bluff too?
If it is, you're one hell of a gambler.
Still, I bet you couldn't beat Okura.{p}

...Huh? That's not what I said before?
I told you Okura was hopeless at gambling?
Yeah, that's right.
He was hopeless... up until a certain point.
But it's no use now.
Nobody can beat him.
No matter what they do.
He was harmless enough back when he was lousy at gambling.
But one day, out of nowhere, he got good.{p}

"This...?
I bought it at an antique shop in my neighborhood.
A real find."
That was all Okura said before he buried himself in the game again.{p}

But once I'd heard that, I had no more use for him.
I headed straight for the antique shop.
If he'd suddenly gotten good, it had to be because of those cards.
If I got my hands on the same thing, maybe I'd get good at gambling too, right?{p}

Finding the antique shop was easy.
It was tucked one street back from the main road, though.
I've got a nose for that kind of thing.
It was a cramped, gloomy little shop.
Dusty pots and Buddhist statues were lined up, looking like they'd been sitting there for hundreds of years.
And mixed in with all that, there it was.
A deck of those skull playing cards.{p}

Same size, same make.
The only difference was that the skull was a man's.
Okura's cards had a skull on the left half and a pale woman on the other, right?
Mine were the reverse: skull on the right, a man's face on the left.
Anyway, I bought them, happy as could be.
But the old man who ran the shop said something weird.
"If you ever come across its lover, never, ever put the two together."
...Something like that.
I didn't think much of it at the time.{p}So, do you think I got good at gambling after that?
You got good at it
Nothing changed

Yeah, I got good, all right.
Once I started using those cards, I won game after game.
It was like the cards understood who their master was and were trying to make him win.
Word must've gotten around eventually.
Okura came to see me.{p}

His face changed when he saw my cards.
He probably never imagined there was another deck like his.
So he said to me:
"Let's play for each other's cards."
I took him up on it.
Think I was an idiot, when one slip and I'd lose my cards?
But if I won, I could take Okura down a peg.
If that's how I think, maybe I'm a born gambler.{p}

Here were the rules.
First, the game was poker.
We'd swap decks, and one of us would shuffle and deal.
Then the other one would pick his cards while they were still face down.
Pretty fair, right?
Even so, the wins would probably come out about fifty-fifty.
So we decided that the moment it stopped being a draw, whoever was ahead would take both decks.
First, Okura dealt with my cards.
Of course, I won.
Sure enough, those cards knew who their master was.
Next I dealt with Okura's cards, and Okura won, naturally.
Things stayed even for a while.
But a few games in, Okura grinned.
It was my deck's turn, so there was no way he could win.{p}

In fact, my hand that time was four kings.
I laid it down, totally confident.
But then he showed me his hand, looking thrilled.
And what do you think it was?{p}

Four aces and a joker.
Five of a kind, aces!
The skull on the joker looked like it was sneering at me.
Grinning, Okura raked in both decks.{p}

No way he could.
He was dead.
...Apparently, when Okura didn't get up in the morning, his family went to check on him.
And there was Okura, dead on his bed.
In a gruesome state.
His body didn't have a scratch on it, but the skin of his head had peeled off, and even the flesh underneath was gone, clean, like it had melted away.
In other words, from the neck up, he'd turned into a skull.{p}
Just like the joker on those cards.{p}

Oh yeah, both decks were in Okura's room.
But the pictures on the backs, which should've been half skull, had changed at some point.
Into a chimera, with a woman's face on the right half and a man's face on the left.
That's what the old man at the shop had been worried about.
The two decks were lovers, and I guess they wanted to be together.
...Now, can you figure out where Okura's face went?
Even the dullest person would get it by now.
The skull woman, the skull man, and Okura.
There were three faces, and three minus two is one.
That's right, the other deck.
On its back was the face of a man nobody had seen there before.
To me, it looked exactly like Okura...{p}Well, that's the end of my story.
Let's move on to the sixth one.{p}

That's right.
I didn't get any better at all.
But hey, I was the one who'd decided on my own that they'd make me good at gambling.
Couldn't exactly go complain to the shop, right?
Still not satisfied, I stopped using those cards.{p}

Then one day, Okura came to see me.
He wanted me to show him my cards.
I guess somebody'd told him they looked like his.
When I showed him, his face changed.
Then he asked me to sell them to him.
He must've figured they had the same power as his, which they didn't.{p}

Of course I sold them to him.
I never said they were cards that'd make you good at gambling.
Okura just assumed it on his own.
All I did was the same thing the old man at the antique shop did.
But then, the moment I handed over the cards for the money.
The eyes of the man in the picture glinted.
And his little mouth moved, too.
"Repayment begins."
That's what it said, I swear.{p}

From the next day on, Okura was lousy at gambling again.
No, maybe even worse than before.
He got so worked up trying to win it back, he sank deeper and deeper.
Even coughing up all the money he'd stashed away wasn't enough.
Eventually even Okura gave up gambling.
But that wasn't the end of it.
A while after that, Okura's dad's company went bankrupt.
On top of that, his dad had co-signed somebody's loan or something, so he got stuck paying that off too.
In the end, Okura dropped out of school.
He's probably working somewhere right about now.
Anyway, about that word 'repayment' the man on the cards said back then.
Don't you think it meant taking back from Okura exactly as much money as he'd won with the woman's cards?
That's why nothing happened to me, I think.
But look at it the other way, and it means Okura raked in that much, right?
...When you put it like that, it's hard to feel too sorry for him.
Oh well.
When you play cards, you'd better check the pictures on the backs carefully too.{p}That's the end of my story.
Next, if you please... as they say.{p}

"This...?
From a festival.
I bought it at a stall."
Okura said it like I was bugging him.
What a curt answer.
Maybe he was focused on the game, but it was like I wasn't even there.{p}

"This...?
I found it."
That's what Okura said.
But I didn't miss how he hesitated for a second before answering.
Okura was lying.
I mean, would you believe a whole deck of cards was just lying around, complete?
And it wasn't even dirty.
But why would he need to lie?
I figured something was fishy.
So I decided to keep an eye on him for a while.{p}

He started searching desperately for someone to play.
Like he couldn't stay alive unless he played poker.
But everyone knew how good he was.
Nobody would take him on.
And then, get this!
He started throwing money around.{p}

If you beat Okura, you'd get prize money.
And even if you lost, you didn't have to pay a thing.
That's insane, right?
But thanks to that, people started playing him.
Of course, Okura was good.
He never lost a single yen.
And when that happens, some people get obsessed.
There was this guy who'd go straight to Okura the minute he got to school in the morning.
His name was Kobayashi or something.{p}

Anyway, apart from class time, it was poker from morning till night.
It wore me out just watching.
But Okura looked happy.
He never got tired of it, playing game after game, hundreds, thousands of times.
Then, one Monday.{p}

Kobayashi didn't come to school.
That surprised me.
By then, Kobayashi had lost interest in everything but poker.
I couldn't believe a little cold would keep him from coming to play.
When I asked Okura, he said they'd spent all weekend playing poker at his place.
Would a guy who'd been that lively the day before just suddenly collapse?
But that's exactly what happened.{p}

According to someone who went to see him, Kobayashi was terribly weak.
Dry, papery skin and sunken eyes.
Over half his hair had gone white, and it was falling out in clumps.
So he ended up being admitted to a hospital far away.{p}

That left Okura in a bind.
He had to find another poker partner, after all.
But after what happened to Kobayashi, none of us felt like it.
We thought Okura might've done something to him.
Okura was getting desperate.
In the end, he said he'd give a thousand yen a game just for playing poker with him.
Who offers a shady deal like that?
Creeped out, everyone started keeping their distance.{p}

Then one day, Okura caught me.
He begged me to play poker with him, just one game, anything.
He looked ready to get down on his hands and knees.
But I said no.
And then...{p}
And then he collapsed.{p}

I rushed over to look, and his eyes had rolled back and he was twitching.
I knew right away it was bad.
Then the life went out of him.
Like a light inside him being switched off with a click.
I guess that was the moment he died.
When people die, they go just that easily, like flipping a switch.
Then, out of his back as he lay face down, something slipped out.
It was hazy, and once it was all the way out of Okura, it took on a solid shape.
What do you think it was?{p}

A big face, half woman and half skull.
That's right, same as the picture on Okura's cards.
It looked at me and grinned wide.
And then it slowly seeped away.
Like it was dissolving into the air.{p}

...Okura was already gone.
When I lifted him up, cards spilled out of his breast pocket.
And get this... can you believe it?
The backs were completely blank.
The skull woman that should've been drawn on them had vanished from every single card.
...Maybe that skull woman was a goddess of gambling.
Or a demon.
Maybe Okura had made a pact with a demon.
That would kinda explain what happened to Kobayashi, too.
...And that's where my story ends.
If there's any part you didn't get, it's not because I'm bad at telling it.
If anybody can explain it, I'd love to hear it myself.
Anyway, that's about it.{p}So, that brings us to number six.
Who was it again...?{p}

Yeah, Okura stopped coming to school.
Worse, he stopped coming out of his room at all.
His family got worried and peeked in, and there he was, sleeping on a bed he'd covered with cards.
Looking blissful, like it felt real good.
But he didn't seem sick, so apparently they just left him alone.{p}

If they left food outside his room, he seemed to eat it, too.
But then one day.
There'd been a death among their relatives, so Okura's whole family had to go away.
His mother called through the door.
"I'm leaving ten thousand yen, so order yourself some takeout."
...Well, it was probably something like that.
Moms everywhere say the same stuff.
And then they left.{p}

Apparently they stayed two nights before coming home.
But the money was just as they'd left it.
The edges had been torn ragged, but anyway, it was right where they'd put it.
They got worried and went to Okura's room.{p}

On the bed was a skeleton.
And scurrying around between the bones were those half-skull women from the cards.
They were about the size of ping-pong balls, and under their heads was a dense mass of tiny tentacles.
That's how they got around.
With their little teeth, they were gnawing at the scraps of flesh still stuck to the bones.
His family screamed.
At the sound, the women all turned around at once.
And then, at incredible speed, they fled out the window.
Like the tide going out, in one big rush.{p}

Why didn't Okura try to get away?
How should I know.
Maybe those women had him under their spell.
But I wonder where the ones that got out of the cards are now.
When I think things like that might be lurking around, the dark scares me.
...Go ahead and laugh.
Anyway, that's the end of my story.{p}Let's hurry up and get the next one over with too.
It's already dark outside.{p}
Hunted for poker partners
Went hard on loan-sharking
Stopped coming to school
